exposure: Previous lower segment cesarean section (LSCS) history
cohort: The study included 70 pregnant women, divided equally into those with a history of previous lower segment cesarean section and those with previous vaginal deliveries, admitted after 28 weeks of gestation.
finding: Women with a history of LSCS experienced higher rates of postpartum hemorrhage and wound sepsis, required more neonatal resuscitation, and their newborns had a significantly lower mean birth weight compared to those with previous vaginal deliveries.
mod_finding: Women with a history of previous LSCS exhibited worse maternal outcomes, including higher rates of postpartum hemorrhage and wound sepsis, and their newborns had a significantly lower mean birth weight, indicating increased risks with a history of cesarean deliveries.
birth_weight: Mean birth weight of 2.81 kg in the LSCS group and 2.87 kg in the control group.
gest_age: Mothers included if admitted after 28 weeks of gestation.
